scope: 31 public native symbols on the 4 xray_semantic modules that still export public native surface

manifest_field_semantics.public_native: MUST equal (non-internal entries parsed out of stdlib/defs/core.def for this module) UNION manual_public_native. It is a derived assertion, not a free-form list.
manifest_field_semantics.manual_public_native: The subset of public_native that does NOT come from core.def at all, i.e. names the C factory registers directly with xr_module_add_export. Each entry is additionally verified to appear as a quoted string literal inside the module's factory_source (checker lines 334-339).
manifest_field_semantics.relationship_for_sync: NOT two different things and NOT redundant: sync has no `module sync {` block in core.def at all (verified). def_public_symbols('sync') is empty, so public_native == manual_public_native is the only value that satisfies the equality. The duplication is an artifact of the equality check, not a second policy.

is_internal_derivation.StdlibMethodEntry: visibility == 'internal'; visibility defaults to 'internal' when the name starts with '__' (stdlibgen.py:593-594). So `fn __x` drops out of public_native.
is_internal_derivation.StdlibConstEntry: HAS NO is_internal property (stdlibgen.py:125-143). getattr(..., 'is_internal', False) is always False, so EVERY core.def const is unconditionally public_native, even if it were named __x.
is_internal_derivation.StdlibNativeClassEntry: HAS NO is_internal property (stdlibgen.py:265-276). Same consequence: renaming NetConn to __NetConn would NOT remove it from public_native.
is_internal_derivation.StdlibClassMethodEntry: HAS NO is_internal property (stdlibgen.py:293-304). Same consequence.
is_internal_derivation.StdlibHandleEntry / StdlibObjectShapeEnt: is_internal = name.startswith('__'). This is why os's `handle __ExecResult` is already invisible to public_native and is the working precedent for a wrap-in-.xr migration.

manifest_field_semantics.second_pin: scripts/check_binary_public_native_readiness.py:26-40 (L2_PUBLIC_NATIVE) independently hard-codes the same os/net sets; scripts/check_stdlib_boundary.py:224-241 (check_l2_thinning) is the first. Both must be edited in the same commit as any os or net change.
manifest_field_semantics.inventory_blind_spot: scripts/stdlib_symbol_inventory.py reads core.def, so the 5 sync symbols do NOT appear in its per-symbol rows at all (verified: 44 sync rows, none of them Semaphore/CountdownLatch/EventCount/WorkQueue/ResultGroup). Any gate built on that inventory is blind to them.

Redeclaring the name in .xr aborts the semantic-plan stage with XR_SEM_0002.
slices.recommendation: Reclassify rather than migrate. sync.c is a 54-line namespace re-export of runtime primitives that sit on the same footing as Array/Map/Set/Channel/Atomic. Either (a) record them as prelude-level runtime primitives outside the stdlib public_native ledger, or (b) accept them as a permanent, per-symbol-approved native surface. Both options are manifest/checker edits, not compiler work.

experiments.question: Does AOT already reject a program importing os?
experiments.result: Error: product Program TargetPlan build failed: XR_TARGET_1000: product TargetPlan requires one canonical program authority
experiments.conclusion: AOT is blocked at baseline for every .xr-sourced stdlib module; the os slice cannot regress it. Confirmed independently by tests/diff/known_failures_not_comparable.txt:426.

experiments.question: Can a module-level `export const` be initialized by a function call and consumed across a module boundary?
experiments.code: plat.xr: import os / fn _sepFor(p: string) -> string { if (p == "windows") { return "\\" } return "/" } / export const PLATFORM: string = os.platform / export const CWD: string = os.getcwd() / export const SEP: string = _sepFor(PLATFORM)   ---   main.xr imports and prints them
experiments.conclusion: The exact shape slice 1 needs works at RUNTIME in the VM.

experiments.question: Does the analyzer accept a module-level const initialized by a SAME-MODULE private native inside stdlib/os/os.xr?
experiments.method: Copied stdlib/ to scratch, appended `export const probeCwd: string = __getcwd()` plus derived consts, ran with XRAY_STDLIB_PATH pointed at the copy.
experiments.negative_control: Appending `export const deliberateTypeError: i64 = __getcwd()` produced: '.../stdlibcopy/os/os.xr:64:14: error: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'i64'' — proving the analyzer really reads the overridden copy.
experiments.caveat: XRAY_STDLIB_PATH steers the ANALYZER only; the VM still executes embedded bytecode (XR_STDLIB_FROM_FILE=OFF in build/CMakeCache.txt). Runtime execution of the new stdlib top-level code was NOT observed and needs a rebuild to confirm. E2 is the runtime evidence for the equivalent shape.

experiments.question: Does an .xr const named the same as a core.def const conflict?
experiments.method: Appended `export const platform/arch/sep/eol` to the copied stdlib/os/os.xr while core.def still declares them.
experiments.result: compiled; a consumer doing len(os.platform), len(os.sep) etc. type-checked and ran; negative control `var n: i64 = os.sep` correctly failed with "Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'i64'".
experiments.conclusion: The .xr declaration wins in module scope. Slice 1 is not blocked by a name collision, and it can be staged .xr-first before the core.def deletion.

experiments.question: Are the 5 sync classes reachable outside stdlib/sync/sync.xr?
experiments.code: const s = Semaphore(1) ... WorkQueue<i64>(2,2) ... ResultGroup(1)   (no import)
experiments.result: error[E0365]: undefined type 'WorkQueue' / error[E0365]: undefined type 'ResultGroup' / error[E0351]: Undeclared variable 'Semaphore' / 'CountdownLatch' / 'EventCount' / 'WorkQueue' / 'ResultGroup'
experiments.conclusion: Not prelude-visible. Their in-sync.xr visibility comes from the hard-coded path gate at src/frontend/analyzer/xanalyzer.c:1931-1939.

experiments.question: Can .xr declare a class named Semaphore?
experiments.code: export final class Semaphore { _n: i64  constructor(n: i64) { this._n = n }  tryAcquire() -> bool { return this._n > 0 } }
experiments.result: [xcompiler] Xi IR pipeline failed at semantic-plan: XR_SEM_0002: builtin type identity is not exact (func=<main>)
experiments.conclusion: Blocked, and blocked badly — the analyzer lets it through and the IR pipeline aborts at the plan stage instead of producing a clean E0350 like NetConn does. Diagnostic-quality defect in its own right.

experiments.question: Can .xr declare a class named NetConn?
experiments.code: export final class NetConn { _fd: i64  constructor(fd: i64) { this._fd = fd }  fd() -> i64 { return this._fd } }
experiments.result: error[E0350]: class 'NetConn' redeclares the builtin 'NetConn' — builtin names are reserved, choose a different name
experiments.conclusion: The native class name must be freed (renamed to __NetConn) before .xr can own the public name. Clean diagnostic, unlike E6.

experiments.question: Can .xr declare the cluster object shapes and enums, and the NetError enum?
experiments.code: import cluster / export enum ClusterDelivery { Accepted, ... Disconnected }   ||   import net / export enum NetError { Timeout, ... OutOfMemory }   ||   import cluster / three nested classes ClusterTlsStatus + ClusterNodeInfo + ClusterInfo with an Array<ClusterNodeInfo> field
experiments.result: delivery ok=true   /   neterror ok=true   /   info ok=a,1,true
experiments.conclusion: All six generated_descriptor type names are FREE — .xr can own them today. Their migration is a C-side construction problem, not a compiler capability problem.

experiments.question: Can an .xr class hold a native handle field (the ExecResult-style wrapper the net migration needs)?
experiments.code: import net / export final class Conn { _h: NetConn  constructor(h: NetConn) { this._h = h }  fd() -> i64 { return net.fd(this._h) } ... }  plus a Channel<i64>-field class
experiments.conclusion: The wrapper shape itself is supported. What is missing is only the ability to take over the public name.

experiments.question: Do the two ways of reaching sync.Semaphore behave the same?
experiments.code: import sync / import { Semaphore } from sync / var a = Semaphore(2); a.tryAcquire() x3  /  var b = sync.Semaphore(2); b.tryAcquire() x2
experiments.result: named a1=true, a2=true, a3=false  |  ns b1=false, ns b2=false  |  CountdownLatch behaves identically both ways
experiments.conclusion: DEFECT, pre-existing and unrelated to migration: namespace-qualified construction sync.Semaphore(n) drops the permit-count argument and yields a 0-permit semaphore, while the named-import form is correct. Only Semaphore is affected among the two tested.

defects_found_in_passing.what: os.arch has two divergent C tables; the VM one cannot report ppc64/loongarch64/riscv64 that LANGUAGE_SPEC.md:6623 documents.
get_platform has an unreachable duplicated branch: `#elif defined(XR_OS_BSD) return "freebsd"` followed by `#elif defined(XR_OS_BSD) return "openbsd"` — openbsd is dead.
sync.Semaphore(n).tryAcquire() is false for any n; the named-import form is correct. See experiment E10.
Redeclaring a sync builtin name in .xr aborts at semantic-plan with XR_SEM_0002 instead of the clean E0350 that NetConn produces. See E6/E7.
declared `(): ()` but the C returns a bool; discovery start/failure is silently discarded.
declared return type is non-nullable Channel but the C returns null on five failure paths.
cluster_info_fn leaks node_arr and partially built instances on three early-return-under-lock paths.
cluster_nodes claims to list connected nodes but lists all of them, and allocates VM objects inside nodes_lock.
three spellings of isClosed; the VM class method omits the fd < 0 check.
the AOT close path calls shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR) before closing; the VM path does not.
the cgen hard-codes log.DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL integer constants that do not exist in stdlib/log/log.xr at all (log.xr uses a LogLevel enum) — apparently dead.
topic grammar validation and matching are implemented twice, independently, in Xray and in C.
the per-symbol inventory reads core.def and therefore cannot see the 5 sync manual_public_native symbols at all.

os.c bypasses the project's XR_ARCH_* macros for raw __aarch64__/__x86_64__/_M_ARM64. This is the stdlib-side twin of the _WIN32-vs-XR_OS_* contract violation the concurrent blocker packet flags in src/aot/xrt_os.h, and it is the mechanical reason the two arch tables drifted.

open_questions: Runtime execution of a stdlib .xr module-level native call was not observed (E3 caveat). Confirming it requires a rebuild, which this investigation did not perform.

Whether an .xr-declared enum reproduces the same nominal layout id that the generated AOT method rows bake in (ClusterDelivery 4282747530, NetError 2184710811) — needs confirmation before slices 3 and 4.
